Vulnerabilities.Title: MLflow vulnerable to remote code execution on unauthenticated servers via third-party scorer deserialization importing caller-placed artifact modules
Vulnerabilities.Description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py accepts request-selected descendants of THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES rather than requiring an exact allowed module. A caller can use MLflow artifact endpoints to place a Python module beneath a writable allowed package and submit its module and class through /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke. Scorer.model_validate_json() imports the module and constructs the class before trace processing. Authentication-disabled deployments permit this code execution without credentials, while basic-auth deployments require a principal capable of creating an experiment and run and uploading artifacts. In either configuration, the allowed scorer package must be writable by the server process. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mlflow: mlflow: Information disclosure via improper path validation in model artifact locations
Vulnerabilities.Description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.10.0 until 3.17.0, the prompt branch in _create_model_version() accepts schemeless relative sources because path validation runs only when a source has a URL scheme, and mlflow.prompt.is_prompt is interpreted by tag presence rather than a true value. A remote caller can store a server-local path as the model version artifact location and use /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/get-artifact to read files accessible to the MLflow server process. Default unauthenticated servers require no privileges, while basic-auth deployments are exposed to authenticated users who can create registered models. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mlflow: mlflow: Arbitrary file write via FileStore path traversal
Vulnerabilities.Description: MLflow 3.17.1 and earlier contains a path traversal vulnerability in the FileStore tracking backend that allows unauthenticated attackers to control filesystem paths by submitting a crafted trace ID containing traversal sequences to the POST /api/3.0/mlflow/traces endpoint. Attackers can exploit FileStore.start_trace() to write trace_info.yaml, request_metadata, and tag files with attacker-controlled metadata outside the intended experiment trace directory, subject to the server process's filesystem permissions. FileStore is the default tracking backend before MLflow 3.7.0 and opt-in thereafter (the default changed to a SQLite database), so deployments in the earlier part of the affected range are vulnerable without special configuration while later ones are affected only when FileStore is explicitly selected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mlflow: mlflow: Server-Side Request Forgery via insecure scorer deserialization
Vulnerabilities.Description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, the scorer invoke, register, and GenAI evaluate endpoints, including unauthenticated POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke, accept serialized third-party scorer data that Scorer.model_validate_json resolves using a module-path allowlist without constraining the selected class or its constructor arguments. When optional trulens and trulens-providers-litellm packages are installed, an attacker can select mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens, choose a model URI outside MLflow's native provider registry so execution uses the LiteLLM fallback, and supply api_base and api_key values that cause the server to send an outbound request to an attacker-chosen or internal host with attacker-controlled headers and body. The vulnerable deserialization occurs before a tracking-store lookup or job submission. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: MLflow CrewAI autologging records LLM provider API keys in logged trace spans
Vulnerabilities.Description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 2.19.0 until 3.17.0, mlflow.crewai.autolog() records CrewAI Agent objects without consistently sanitizing nested credential-bearing values. mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_get_agent_attributes() converts the Agent llm field to a string that includes the provider API key, while mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_construct_full_inputs() expands the Agent object into mlflow.spanInputs. Applications can therefore send plaintext provider credentials to the MLflow trace backend or a configured OTLP destination, where trace readers can obtain them. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: apache-arrow: Apache Arrow C++: Denial of Service via Use After Free vulnerability when reading IPC files
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Use After Free vulnerability in Apache Arrow C++.

This issue affects Apache Arrow C++ from 15.0.0 through 23.0.0. It can be triggered when reading an Arrow IPC file (but not an IPC stream) with pre-buffering enabled, if the IPC file contains data with variadic buffers (such as Binary View and String View data). Depending on the number of variadic buffers in a record batch column and on the temporal sequence of multi-threaded IO, a write to a dangling pointer could occur. The value (a `std::shared_ptr<Buffer>` object) that is written to the dangling pointer is not under direct control of the attacker.

Pre-buffering is disabled by default but can be enabled using a specific C++ API call (`RecordBatchFileReader::PreBufferMetadata`). The functionality is not exposed in language bindings (Python, Ruby, C GLib), so these bindings are not vulnerable.

The most likely consequence of this issue would be random crashes or memory corruption when reading specific kinds of IPC files. If the application allows ingesting IPC files from untrusted sources, this could plausibly be exploited for denial of service. Inducing more targeted kinds of misbehavior (such as confidential data extraction from the running process) depends on memory allocation and multi-threaded IO temporal patterns that are unlikely to be easily controlled by an attacker.

Advice for users of Arrow C++:

1. check whether you enable pre-buffering on the IPC file reader (using `RecordBatchFileReader::PreBufferMetadata`)

2. if so, either disable pre-buffering (which may have adverse performance consequences), or switch to Arrow 23.0.1 which is not vulnerable

Vulnerabilities.Title: Dask distributed is a distributed task scheduler for Dask. Prior to 20 ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: Dask distributed is a distributed task scheduler for Dask. Prior to 2026.1.0, when Jupyter Lab, jupyter-server-proxy, and Dask distributed are all run together, it is possible to craft a URL which will result in code being executed by Jupyter due to a cross-side-scripting (XSS) bug in the Dask dashboard. It is possible for attackers to craft a phishing URL that assumes Jupyter Lab and Dask may be running on localhost and using default ports. If a user clicks on the malicious link it will open an error page in the Dask Dashboard via the Jupyter Lab proxy which will cause code to be executed by the default Jupyter Python kernel. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.1.0.

Advice for users of Arrow C++:

1. check whether you enable pre-buffering on the IPC file reader (using `RecordBatchFileReader::PreBufferMetadata`)

Misconfigurations.Title: ':latest' tag used
Misconfigurations.Description: When using a 'FROM' statement you should use a specific tag to avoid uncontrolled behavior when the image is updated.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a tag to the image in the 'FROM' statement

Misconfigurations.Title: Image user should not be 'root'
Misconfigurations.Description: Running containers with 'root' user can lead to a container escape situation. It is a best practice to run containers as non-root users, which can be done by adding a 'USER' statement to the Dockerfile.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add 'USER <non root user name>' line to the Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: Port 22 exposed
Misconfigurations.Description: Exposing port 22 might allow users to SSH into the container.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove 'EXPOSE 22' statement from the Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: ADD instead of COPY
Misconfigurations.Description: You should use COPY instead of ADD unless you want to extract a tar file. Note that an ADD command will extract a tar file, which adds the risk of Zip-based vulnerabilities. Accordingly, it is advised to use a COPY command, which does not extract tar files.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use COPY instead of ADD

Misconfigurations.Title: COPY '--from' referring to the current image
Misconfigurations.Description: COPY '--from' should not mention the current FROM alias, since it is impossible to copy from itself.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Change the '--from' so that it will not refer to itself

Misconfigurations.Title: Multiple ENTRYPOINT instructions listed
Misconfigurations.Description: There can only be one ENTRYPOINT instruction in a Dockerfile. Only the last ENTRYPOINT instruction in the Dockerfile will have an effect.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove unnecessary ENTRYPOINT instruction.

Misconfigurations.Title: Exposed port out of range
Misconfigurations.Description: UNIX ports outside the range 0-65535 are exposed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use port number within range

Misconfigurations.Title: WORKDIR path not absolute
Misconfigurations.Description: For clarity and reliability, you should always use absolute paths for your WORKDIR.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use absolute paths for your WORKDIR

Misconfigurations.Title: RUN using 'sudo'
Misconfigurations.Description: Avoid using 'RUN' with 'sudo' commands, as it can lead to unpredictable behavior.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Don't use sudo

Misconfigurations.Title: COPY with more than two arguments not ending with slash
Misconfigurations.Description: When a COPY command has more than two arguments, the last one should end with a slash.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add slash to last COPY argument

Misconfigurations.Title: Duplicate aliases defined in different FROMs
Misconfigurations.Description: Different FROMs can't have the same alias defined.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Change aliases to make them different

Misconfigurations.Title: 'RUN cd ...' to change directory
Misconfigurations.Description: Use WORKDIR instead of proliferating instructions like 'RUN cd … && do-something', which are hard to read, troubleshoot, and maintain.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use WORKDIR to change directory

Misconfigurations.Title: RUN using 'wget' and 'curl'
Misconfigurations.Description: Avoid using both 'wget' and 'curl' since these tools have the same effect.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Pick one util, either 'wget' or 'curl'

Misconfigurations.Title: 'yum clean all' missing
Misconfigurations.Description: You should use 'yum clean all' after using a 'yum install' command to clean package cached data and reduce image size.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add 'yum clean all' to Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: Multiple CMD instructions listed
Misconfigurations.Description: There can only be one CMD instruction in a Dockerfile. If you list more than one CMD then only the last CMD will take effect.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Dockerfile should only have one CMD instruction. Remove all the other CMD instructions

Misconfigurations.Title: 'RUN <package-manager> update' instruction alone
Misconfigurations.Description: The instruction 'RUN <package-manager> update' should always be followed by '<package-manager> install' in the same RUN statement.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Combine '<package-manager> update' and '<package-manager> install' instructions to single one

Misconfigurations.Title: 'dnf clean all' missing
Misconfigurations.Description: Cached package data should be cleaned after installation to reduce image size.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add 'dnf clean all' to Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: 'zypper clean' missing
Misconfigurations.Description: The layer and image size should be reduced by deleting unneeded caches after running zypper.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add 'zypper clean' to Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: 'apt-get' missing '-y' to avoid manual input
Misconfigurations.Description: 'apt-get' calls should use the flag '-y' to avoid manual user input.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add '-y' flag to 'apt-get'

Misconfigurations.Title: Deprecated MAINTAINER used
Misconfigurations.Description: MAINTAINER has been deprecated since Docker 1.13.0.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use LABEL instead of MAINTAINER

Misconfigurations.Title: Multiple HEALTHCHECK defined
Misconfigurations.Description: Providing more than one HEALTHCHECK instruction per stage is confusing and error-prone.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: One HEALTHCHECK instruction must remain in Dockerfile. Remove all other instructions.

Misconfigurations.Title: 'apk add' is missing '--no-cache'
Misconfigurations.Description: You should use 'apk add' with '--no-cache' to clean package cached data and reduce image size.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add '--no-cache' to 'apk add' in Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: No HEALTHCHECK defined
Misconfigurations.Description: You should add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your docker container images to perform the health check on running containers.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction in Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: 'microdnf clean all' missing
Misconfigurations.Description: Cached package data should be cleaned after installation to reduce image size.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add 'microdnf clean all' to Dockerfile

Misconfigurations.Title: 'apt-get' missing '--no-install-recommends'
Misconfigurations.Description: 'apt-get' install should use '--no-install-recommends' to minimize image size.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add '--no-install-recommends' flag to 'apt-get'

Misconfigurations.Title: WORKDIR should not be mounted on system dirs
Misconfigurations.Description: WORKDIR should not be mounted on system directories to avoid container breakouts
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Avoid using system directories to mount WORKDIR

Misconfigurations.Title: Secrets passed via `build-args` or envs or copied secret files
Misconfigurations.Description: Passing secrets via `build-args` or envs or copying secret files can leak them out
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use secret mount if secrets are needed during image build. Use volume mount if secret files are needed during container runtime.

Misconfigurations.Title: Config configuration aggregator should be using all regions for source
Misconfigurations.Description:
Sources that aren't covered by the aggregator are not include in the configuration. The configuration aggregator should be configured with all_regions for the source.
This will help limit the risk of any unmonitored configuration in regions that are thought to be unused.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set the aggregator to cover all regions

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should prevent password reuse.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should prevent the reuse of passwords.

The account password policy should be set to prevent using any of the last five used passwords.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Prevent password reuse in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one lowercase character.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one lowercase character.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one number in the password.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one number.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one symbol in the password.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including a symbol.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one uppercase character.
Misconfigurations.Description:
,

IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one uppercase character.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have expiry less than or equal to 90 days.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should have a maximum age specified.

The account password policy should be set to expire passwords after 90 days or less.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit the password duration with an expiry in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have minimum password length of 14 or more characters.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords have a minimum length.

The account password policy should be set to enforce minimum password length of at least 14 characters.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM groups should have MFA enforcement activated.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM groups should be protected with multi factor authentication to add safe guards to password compromise.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use terraform-module/enforce-mfa/aws to ensure that MFA is enforced

Misconfigurations.Title: The "root" account has unrestricted access to all resources in the AWS account. It is highly recommended that the use of this account be avoided.
Misconfigurations.Description: The root user has unrestricted access to all services and resources in an AWS account. We highly recommend that you avoid using the root user for daily tasks. Minimizing the use of the root user and adopting the principle of least privilege for access management reduce the risk of accidental changes and unintended disclosure of highly privileged credentials.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use lower privileged accounts instead, so only required privileges are available.

Misconfigurations.Title: The root user has complete access to all services and resources in an AWS account. AWS Access Keys provide programmatic access to a given account.
Misconfigurations.Description: CIS recommends that all access keys be associated with the root user be removed. Removing access keys associated with the root user limits vectors that the account can be compromised by. Removing the root user access keys also encourages the creation and use of role-based accounts that are least privileged.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use lower privileged accounts instead, so only required privileges are available.

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM policies should not be granted directly to users.
Misconfigurations.Description: CIS recommends that you apply IAM policies directly to groups and roles but not users. Assigning privileges at the group or role level reduces the complexity of access management as the number of users grow. Reducing access management complexity might in turn reduce opportunity for a principal to inadvertently receive or retain excessive privileges.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Grant policies at the group level instead.

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Pass Role Filtering
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures any IAM pass role attached to roles are flagged and warned.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Resolve permission escalations by denying pass role'

Misconfigurations.Title: Disallow unrestricted S3 IAM Policies
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensure that the creation of the unrestricted S3 IAM policies is disallowed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create more restrictive S3 policies

Misconfigurations.Title: Reduce unnecessary unauthorized access or information disclosure of S3 buckets.
Misconfigurations.Description: Unnecessary access to S3 buckets can lead to unauthorized access or information disclosure.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Allowing Get* along with Put* on all Resources can potentially allow unauthorized access and/or information disclosure from sensitive buckets.

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage containers in blob storage mode should not have public access
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage container public access should be off. It can be configured for blobs only, containers and blobs or off entirely. The default is off, with no public access.
Explicitly overriding publicAccess to anything other than off should be avoided.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable public access to storage containers

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage accounts should be configured to only accept transfers that are over secure connections
Misconfigurations.Description:
You can configure your storage account to accept requests from secure connections only by setting the Secure transfer required property for the storage account.
When you require secure transfer, any requests originating from an insecure connection are rejected.
Microsoft recommends that you always require secure transfer for all of your storage accounts.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Only allow secure connection for transferring data into storage accounts

Misconfigurations.Title: When using Queue Services for a storage account, logging should be enabled.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.
This information can be used to monitor individual requests and to diagnose issues with a storage service.
Requests are logged on a best-effort basis.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for Queue Services

Misconfigurations.Description:
Some Microsoft services that interact with storage accounts operate from networks that can't be granted access through network rules.
To help this type of service work as intended, allow the set of trusted Microsoft services to bypass the network rules
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Allow Trusted Microsoft Services to bypass

Misconfigurations.Description:
Azure Storage supports four versions of the TLS protocol: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3.
Azure Storage uses TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 on public HTTPS endpoints, while TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are still supported for backward compatibility.
This check will warn if the minimum TLS version is set lower than TLS1_2. TLS1_2 and TLS1_3 are both allowed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use a more recent TLS version for the storage account

Misconfigurations.Title: The default action on Storage account network rules should be set to deny
Misconfigurations.Description:
The default_action for network rules should come into effect when no other rules are matched.
The default action should be set to Deny.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set network rules to deny

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have blob soft delete enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Blob soft delete protects blob data from being accidentally or erroneously modified or deleted.
When blob soft delete is enabled, deleted blobs are retained in the system for a specified retention period.
During the retention period, you can restore a soft-deleted blob to its state at the time it was deleted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable soft delete for blobs with an appropriate retention period

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have logging enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.

Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for at least one storage service (Queue, Table, or Blob)

Options include GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, and RAGZRS for geo-redundancy.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure storage account to use geo-redundant replication (GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, or RAGZRS)

Storage accounts should enforce HTTPS for secure data transfer and use a minimum TLS version of 1.2 or higher.
This ensures that logs and data stored in the storage account are encrypted in transit.
Azure Storage encrypts all data at rest by default, but transport encryption is also critical.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable secure transfer and set minimum TLS version to TLS1_2 or higher

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have infrastructure encryption enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Infrastructure encryption provides an additional layer of encryption at the infrastructure level.
When infrastructure encryption is enabled, data in the storage account is encrypted twice -
once at the service level and once at the infrastructure level with two different encryption algorithms.

Misconfigurations.Title: A firewall rule should not allow unrestricted ingress from any IP address.

Misconfigurations.Title: VPC flow logs should be enabled for all subnetworks
Misconfigurations.Description: VPC flow logs record information about all traffic, which is a vital tool in reviewing anomalous traffic.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable VPC flow logs

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable project-wide SSH keys for all instances
Misconfigurations.Description: Use of project-wide SSH keys means that a compromise of any one of these key pairs can result in all instances being compromised. It is recommended to use instance-level keys.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable project-wide SSH keys

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not have public IP addresses
Misconfigurations.Description: Instances should not be publicly exposed to the internet
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove public IP

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable serial port connectivity for all instances
Misconfigurations.Description: When serial port access is enabled, the access is not governed by network security rules meaning the port can be exposed publicly.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable serial port access

Misconfigurations.Title: VM disks should be encrypted with Customer Supplied Encryption Keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Using unmanaged keys makes rotation and general management difficult.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use managed keys

Misconfigurations.Title: Disks should be encrypted with customer managed encryption keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Using unmanaged keys makes rotation and general management difficult.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use managed keys to encrypt disks.

Misconfigurations.Title: A firewall rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive cidr range

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not override the project setting for OS Login
Misconfigurations.Description: OS Login automatically revokes the relevant SSH keys when an IAM user has their access revoked.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable OS Login at project level and remove instance-level overrides

Misconfigurations.Title: The encryption key used to encrypt a compute disk has been specified in plaintext.
Misconfigurations.Description: Sensitive values such as raw encryption keys should not be included in your Terraform code, and should be stored securely by a secrets manager.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Reference a managed key rather than include the key in raw format.

Misconfigurations.Title: SSL policies should enforce secure versions of TLS
Misconfigurations.Description: TLS versions prior to 1.2 are outdated and insecure. You should use 1.2 as aminimum version.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce a minimum TLS version of 1.2

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM VTPM enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: The virtual TPM provides numerous security measures to your VM.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM VTPM

Misconfigurations.Title: OS Login should be enabled at project level
Misconfigurations.Description: OS Login automatically revokes the relevant SSH keys when an IAM user has their access revoked.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable OS Login at project level

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not have IP forwarding enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Disabling IP forwarding ensures the instance can only receive packets addressed to the instance and can only send packets with a source address of the instance.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable IP forwarding

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not use the default service account
Misconfigurations.Description: The default service account has full project access. Instances should instead be assigned the minimal access they need.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove use of default service account

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM integrity monitoring enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Integrity monitoring helps you understand and make decisions about the state of your VM instances.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM Integrity Monitoring

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM secure boot enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Secure boot helps ensure that the system only runs authentic software.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM secure boot

Misconfigurations.Title: RDP Access Is Not Restricted
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should restrict RDP (TCP/3389) access to specific IP ranges. Open RDP access can be a security risk.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Restrict RDP (TCP port 3389) ingress in firewall rules. Only allow trusted IP ranges or use Identity-Aware Proxy for RDP access.

Misconfigurations.Title: SSH Access Is Not Restricted
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should restrict SSH (TCP/22) access to specific IPs. Open SSH can be a security risk.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Restrict SSH (TCP port 22) access in firewall rules to known IP addresses or ranges. Avoid open 0.0.0.0/0 access for SSH.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Network Using Firewall Rule that Allows All Ports
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should not be wide open to all ports. Lock down rules to only required ports.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Modify firewall rules that allow all ports to restrict to only required ports. Use separate rules for specific port ranges as needed, instead of a single overly broad rule.

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable Default Firewall Rules
Misconfigurations.Description:
Ensures that Google Cloud's default firewall rules are disabled, as they may be overly permissive and pose security risks.
The default network comes with pre-populated firewall rules that allow broad access and should be replaced with more restrictive custom rules.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Replace default firewall rules with custom, more restrictive rules appropriate for your security requirements

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Network Using Firewall Rule that Allows Large Port Range
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules allowing broad port ranges can be risky. Ensure rules are as specific as possible.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit firewall rules to necessary port ranges only. If a wide range is specified, consider splitting into smaller ranges or specific ports needed for your application.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Subnetwork with Private Google Access Disabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Private Google Access allows instances in a subnet to reach Google APIs and services via internal IP, which should be enabled for private networks.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Private Google Access on subnets. In Terraform, set `private_ip_google_access = true` in the `google_compute_subnetwork` resource.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Subnetwork Logging Disabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Flow logs for subnets should be enabled to capture network traffic details for security analysis.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable VPC Flow Logs for subnets.

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage containers in blob storage mode should not have public access
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage container public access should be off. It can be configured for blobs only, containers and blobs or off entirely. The default is off, with no public access.
Explicitly overriding publicAccess to anything other than off should be avoided.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable public access to storage containers

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage accounts should be configured to only accept transfers that are over secure connections
Misconfigurations.Description:
You can configure your storage account to accept requests from secure connections only by setting the Secure transfer required property for the storage account.
When you require secure transfer, any requests originating from an insecure connection are rejected.
Microsoft recommends that you always require secure transfer for all of your storage accounts.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Only allow secure connection for transferring data into storage accounts

Misconfigurations.Title: When using Queue Services for a storage account, logging should be enabled.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.
This information can be used to monitor individual requests and to diagnose issues with a storage service.
Requests are logged on a best-effort basis.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for Queue Services

Misconfigurations.Title: Trusted Microsoft Services should have bypass access to Storage accounts
Misconfigurations.Description:
Some Microsoft services that interact with storage accounts operate from networks that can't be granted access through network rules.
To help this type of service work as intended, allow the set of trusted Microsoft services to bypass the network rules
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Allow Trusted Microsoft Services to bypass

Misconfigurations.Title: The minimum TLS version for Storage Accounts should be TLS1_2 or higher
Misconfigurations.Description:
Azure Storage supports four versions of the TLS protocol: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3.
Azure Storage uses TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 on public HTTPS endpoints, while TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are still supported for backward compatibility.
This check will warn if the minimum TLS version is set lower than TLS1_2. TLS1_2 and TLS1_3 are both allowed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use a more recent TLS version for the storage account

Misconfigurations.Title: The default action on Storage account network rules should be set to deny
Misconfigurations.Description:
The default_action for network rules should come into effect when no other rules are matched.
The default action should be set to Deny.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set network rules to deny

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have blob soft delete enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Blob soft delete protects blob data from being accidentally or erroneously modified or deleted.
When blob soft delete is enabled, deleted blobs are retained in the system for a specified retention period.
During the retention period, you can restore a soft-deleted blob to its state at the time it was deleted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable soft delete for blobs with an appropriate retention period

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have logging enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.
This information can be used to monitor individual requests and to diagnose issues with a storage service.
Logging should be enabled for at least one storage service type.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for at least one storage service (Queue, Table, or Blob)

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should use geo-redundant replication
Misconfigurations.Description:
Geo-redundant storage (GRS) replicates your data to a secondary region that is hundreds of miles away from the primary region.
This provides an additional level of durability for your data in the event of a complete regional outage or a disaster.
Options include GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, and RAGZRS for geo-redundancy.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure storage account to use geo-redundant replication (GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, or RAGZRS)

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have secure transfer and minimum TLS version configured
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage accounts should enforce HTTPS for secure data transfer and use a minimum TLS version of 1.2 or higher.
This ensures that logs and data stored in the storage account are encrypted in transit.
Azure Storage encrypts all data at rest by default, but transport encryption is also critical.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable secure transfer and set minimum TLS version to TLS1_2 or higher

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should use customer-managed keys for encryption
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage accounts should use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption to provide additional control over the encryption keys.
Customer-managed keys allow you to create, rotate, disable, and revoke access controls.
They also provide greater flexibility to audit the encryption keys that are used to protect your data.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure customer-managed keys for storage account encryption

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have infrastructure encryption enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Infrastructure encryption provides an additional layer of encryption at the infrastructure level.
When infrastructure encryption is enabled, data in the storage account is encrypted twice -
once at the service level and once at the infrastructure level with two different encryption algorithms.
This provides double encryption for enhanced security.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable infrastructure encryption for storage account

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should use customer-managed keys for encryption

Storage accounts should use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption to provide additional control over the encryption keys.
Customer-managed keys allow you to create, rotate, disable, and revoke access controls.
They also provide greater flexibility to audit the encryption keys that are used to protect your data.
Misconfigurations.Message: Storage account with blob containers should use customer-managed keys for encryption.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure customer-managed keys for storage account encryption

Misconfigurations.Title: Do not allow role to create ClusterRoleBindings and association with privileged role
Misconfigurations.Description: Check whether role permits creating role ClusterRoleBindings and association with privileged cluster role
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create a role which does not permit to create role clusterrolebindings and associate to privileged cluster role

Misconfigurations.Title: Do not allow attaching to shell on pods
Misconfigurations.Description: Check whether role permits attaching to shell on pods
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create a role which does not permit attaching to shell on pods

Misconfigurations.Title: Do not allow users in a rolebinding to add other users to their rolebindings
Misconfigurations.Description: Check whether role permits allowing users in a rolebinding to add other users to their rolebindings
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create a role which does not permit allowing users in a rolebinding to add other users to their rolebindings if not needed

Misconfigurations.Title: Tiller Is Deployed
Misconfigurations.Description: Check if Helm Tiller component is deployed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Migrate to Helm v3 which no longer has Tiller component

Misconfigurations.Title: Containers must not set runAsUser to 0
Misconfigurations.Description: Containers should be forbidden from running with a root UID.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set 'securityContext.runAsUser' to a non-zero integer or leave undefined.

Misconfigurations.Title: Container capabilities must only include NET_BIND_SERVICE
Misconfigurations.Description: Containers must drop ALL capabilities, and are only permitted to add back the NET_BIND_SERVICE capability.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set 'spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.drop' to 'ALL' and only add 'NET_BIND_SERVICE' to 'spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add'.

Misconfigurations.Title: The deprecated 'apiVersion' and 'kind' should not be used
Misconfigurations.Description: The specified 'apiVersion' and 'kind' are deprecated and are planned to be removed
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Migrate resource to new API

Misconfigurations.Title: Prevent binding to privileged ports
Misconfigurations.Description: The ports which are lower than 1024 receive and transmit various sensitive and privileged data. Allowing containers to use them can bring serious implications.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Do not map the container ports to privileged host ports when starting a container.

Misconfigurations.Title: Gatekeeper repo reference is ambiguously open-ended
Misconfigurations.Description: A Gatekeeper policy that references image repositories for prefix-matching is using open-ended and ambiguous pattern, and can potentially match unintended repositories.
